# Results — Study 382 (Treasury cash-futures Basis Trade)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The hedge-fund **Treasury
basis trade** — buy the cheap cash bond, short the rich future, harvest the **net carry**
at extreme leverage — tested on a **transparent carry / implied-repo MODEL**. True
cash-vs-futures bond prices and GC repo are not free on yfinance, so we build the net carry
as the 10-year yield (`^TNX`) minus a short funding rate (`^IRX`, 13-week T-bill as a repo
proxy), with a small-duration residual mark-to-market. Offline & deterministic; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily closes — `^TNX` (10y yield), `^IRX` (13w bill, repo proxy), `IEF` (cash-leg ETF) |
| As-of | **2026-06-18** (last complete bar; the in-progress 2026-06-22 bar is dropped) |
| Window | 2002-07-31 → 2026-06-18 (**6,004** trading days; **23.8** years) |
| Carry model | net carry = `^TNX − ^IRX` (%/yr); daily carry = net_carry(t−1)/252 (**1-day lag**) |
| Mark-to-market | residual basis wobble = −0.5y × Δ(net carry); the duration-hedged residual |
| Leverage | basis desks run **50–100×** via repo; we report L = 1 / 50 / 100 |

> **Model caveat (named on the Signal axis).** This is an **implied-repo / carry model**,
> not a live cash-vs-futures basis feed. The carry leg is a **term-premium proxy** (10y −
> bill), the funding leg a **repo proxy** (the bill rate tracks GC repo closely *except* in
> acute stress — exactly when the trade blows up, so our tail is if anything *understated*),
> and the residual duration (0.5y) is a transparent, modest choice that scales the tail, not
> the carry. The verdict does not hinge on these knobs: the carry is real at any reasonable
> setting, and Sharpe is leverage-invariant by construction.

## Signal — is the carry real? (everything here is leverage-invariant)

The net carry is positive on **86.5%** of days (mean 10y **3.11%** vs funding **1.68%** ⇒
**1.42%/yr** gross carry). The unlevered basis return earns **+1.47%/yr** at an annualised
**Sharpe of 2.86**. We test the mean daily return with a **Newey-West (HAC, lag = 21)** *t*
and a **sign-randomisation placebo** (flip the carry's sign at random; how often does noise
beat the real Sharpe?).

| statistic | value | bar |
|---|--:|---|
| unlevered annualised return | **+1.47%** | — |
| **HAC (NW, lag 21) *t* of the mean** | **11.71** | ≥ 2 for `REAL` ✅ |
| annualised Sharpe (≈ *t* 13.9) | **2.86** | — |
| sign-flip placebo *p* | **0.000** | < 0.05 ✅ |

The carry is unambiguously real — it survives autocorrelation-robust inference by a mile.
But "real" here means **a real risk premium**: the long bond out-yields short funding because
it bears duration and convergence risk. That is *beta you are paid for*, not free alpha — and
the next section shows what that beta costs at the leverage the trade actually runs.

## Tradability — the SAME Sharpe, levered to where the trade lives

Sharpe is **leverage-invariant**: levering the identical return series multiplies mean *and*
vol together, so the Sharpe does not move — but the **drawdown** and the **tail** explode.

| leverage | ann. return | Sharpe | max drawdown | worst day | 1% CVaR |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1× (cash) | +1.5% | **2.86** | −2.6% | −0.4% | −0.1% |
| **50×** (typical) | +73.4% | **2.86** | **−75.1%** | **−18.5%** | **−5.8%** |
| 100× (aggressive) | +146.9% | **2.86** | **−94.6%** | **−36.9%** | −11.7% |

The "70%/yr free carry" headline is just **the 1.5% term premium multiplied by 50**. The
Sharpe never changes — which is precisely the tell: there is no extra reward for the
leverage, only extra *risk*. At 50× a single bad day is **−18.5%** and the worst drawdown is
**−75%**; at 100× the book is effectively wiped (−95%).

## The tail — why this is short-volatility, not free carry

| diagnostic (unlevered) | value |
|---|--:|
| skew | −0.27 |
| **excess kurtosis** | **9.8** |
| worst single day | −0.369% |
| worst rolling 5-day | −0.706% |

Excess kurtosis of **~10** with negative skew is the fingerprint of a **carry / short-vol**
return: long stretches of smooth positive accrual punctuated by rare, violent losses. The
worst unlevered day is −0.37% — *0.4%* — which sounds trivial until you multiply by 50: at
50× that is **−18.5% in one session**, enough to breach typical haircuts and trigger a
forced unwind.

## Funding-shock stress — March 2020 (the basis trade's near-death)

In March 2020 the cash-futures basis dislocated, repo seized, and levered relative-value
funds were force-unwound — the Fed intervened in part to stop the spiral.

| window | unlevered | **50×** | 100× |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 2020-03-09 → 2020-03-20 (10 trading days) | −0.31% | **−15.8%** | −31.2% |

A −0.31% wobble in the *unlevered* basis becomes a **−16% portfolio hit at 50×** in two
weeks — on top of margin calls that force selling into the very dislocation. This is the
"hidden leverage risk" the believers' "free carry" framing omits.

## Costs barely matter — which is itself the point

| leverage | gross ann. | roll cost (4×/yr, 1 bp one-way × notional) | net ann. |
|---:|--:|--:|--:|
| 50× | +73.4% | −2.0% | **+71.4%** |

A quarterly futures roll at 1 bp shaves ~2%/yr off a 73% gross — costs are **not** the
binding constraint. The trade does not die on the spread; it dies on the **tail × leverage**.

## Synthetic positive control — the engine is faithful, the lesson is mechanical

On a deterministic carry-plus-jump series with a **planted unlevered Sharpe**:

| planted Sharpe | measured Sharpe | HAC *t* | Sharpe(1×) = Sharpe(50×) | maxDD 1× → 50× |
|---:|--:|--:|---|---|
| **0.0** (no edge) | 0.00 | 0.00 | 0.00 = 0.00 | −4% → **−95%** |
| **2.5** (large edge) | 2.50 | 12.80 | 2.50 = 2.50 | −1% → **−58%** |

With **no** planted edge the harness reports Sharpe ≈ 0 and HAC *t* ≈ 0 (it cannot
manufacture an edge from noise) — yet levering that *zero-edge* noise 50× still produces a
−95% drawdown. With a planted Sharpe of 2.5 the inference recovers it exactly. The control
proves both halves of the verdict: the inference is honest, **and** leverage-invariance of
Sharpe alongside an exploding drawdown is mechanical, not an artefact.

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL.** The net carry is genuinely positive and survives HAC inference
  overwhelmingly (NW *t* = **11.71**, sign-flip placebo *p* = **0.000**, Sharpe 2.86). It is
  a **real risk premium** — the term/funding spread — named as a proxy on the model. Real,
  not a mirage; but real *as beta you are paid for*, not as free alpha.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The "70%/yr free carry" is the 1.5% premium **× 50 leverage**;
  the Sharpe is unchanged (no reward for the leverage, only risk), the max drawdown is
  **−75%** at 50× / **−95%** at 100×, and a single bad day is **−18.5%**. A March-2020-style
  funding shock takes **−16%** at 50× in two weeks while margin calls force the unwind. Costs
  are negligible; the **tail × leverage** is fatal. Not a NAV-scale, survivable strategy.
- **"Free carry"? — BUSTED.** The smooth positive accrual hides excess kurtosis of **~10**
  and a funding-tail that only a central-bank backstop has historically absorbed. It is a
  **short-volatility carry on leverage**, not free money — the classic "picking up pennies
  in front of a steamroller," wearing a Treasury costume.
